from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Start with a set of finite points in space.",
            "- A line passes through one point, called the pivot.",
            "- The line rotates clockwise around this pivot point.",
            "- It continues until it hits another point in the set.",
            "- The hit point becomes the new center of rotation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Dancing Line", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_POINTS = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_LINE = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_HIT = "#00FF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # - Start with a set of finite points in space.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_POINTS)
        points_pos = ["C3", "D4", "B2", "B5", "A4", "E2", "E5", "F3", "D1", "A6"]
        points = VGroup()
        for pos in points_pos:
            dot = Dot(color=COLOR_POINTS, radius=0.08)
            self.place_at_grid(dot, pos)
            points.add(dot)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(points))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # - A line passes through one point, called the pivot.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_LINE)
        pivot_point = points[0] # C3
        
        # Create a line long enough to span the local grid area
        line = Line(start=LEFT*3, end=RIGHT*3, color=COLOR_LINE)
        line.move_to(pivot_point.get_center())
        # Initial angle: 120 degrees
        line.rotate(120 * DEGREES) 
        
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # - The line rotates clockwise around this pivot point.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_LINE)
        
        # Target angle calculation for D4 relative to C3
        v = points[1].get_center() - points[0].get_center()
        target_angle_rad = np.arctan2(v[1], v[0])
        current_angle_rad = 120 * DEGREES
        
        # Calculate clockwise rotation angle (negative)
        rot_angle = target_angle_rad - current_angle_rad
        while rot_angle > 0:
            rot_angle -= 2 * PI
            
        self.play(
            Rotate(line, angle=rot_angle, about_point=pivot_point.get_center()),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # - It continues until it hits another point in the set.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_HIT)
        hit_point = points[1]
        
        self.play(
            hit_point.animate.set_color(COLOR_HIT).scale(1.5),
            pivot_point.animate.set_color(COLOR_HIT).scale(1.5)
        )
        self.play(
            Flash(hit_point, color=COLOR_HIT),
            Flash(pivot_point, color=COLOR_HIT),
            hit_point.animate.scale(1/1.5),
            pivot_point.animate.scale(1/1.5)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # - The hit point becomes the new center of rotation.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_LINE) 
        
        # Scale up slightly to emphasize dancing motion
        everything = VGroup(points, line)
        self.play(everything.animate.scale(1.1))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define titles and lines
        title_text = "Prerequisite: General Position & Rotation"
        lecture_lines = [
            "We assume no three points lie on one line.",
            "This ensures the line hits only one point at once.",
            "The line's angle determines its unique position and state."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Use white for point-related concepts
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Initially collinear points B2, C3, D4
        dot1 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        dot2 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        dot3 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(dot1, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(dot2, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(dot3, 'D4')
        
        points_vg = VGroup(dot1, dot2, dot3)
        self.play(Create(points_vg), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Move dot3 to D5 to break collinearity
        self.play(dot3.animate.move_to(self.grid['D5']), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Cyan color for the windmill line
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        pivot_pos = dot2.get_center()
        
        # Rotating line setup
        # Long line to span the right side grid
        rotating_line = Line(
            start=pivot_pos + 4 * LEFT,
            end=pivot_pos + 4 * RIGHT,
            color="#00FFFF"
        )
        
        # Updater for efficient rotation without redrawing the whole mobject
        def line_updater(mob):
            ang = angle_tracker.get_value()
            direction = np.array([np.cos(ang), np.sin(ang), 0])
            mob.set_points_by_ends(
                pivot_pos - 4 * direction,
                pivot_pos + 4 * direction
            )
        
        rotating_line.add_updater(line_updater)
        self.play(Create(rotating_line))
        
        # Calculate angles to hit dot1 and dot3 to demonstrate unique hits
        v1 = dot1.get_center() - pivot_pos
        ang1 = np.arctan2(v1[1], v1[0])
        
        v3 = dot3.get_center() - pivot_pos
        ang3 = np.arctan2(v3[1], v3[0])
        
        # Sweep to hit dot1
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(ang1), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)
        # Sweep to hit dot3
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(ang3), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Yellow for angle arc and Green for Pivot highlight
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Pivot visual cues
        pivot_highlight = Circle(radius=0.15, color="#00FF00").move_to(pivot_pos)
        pivot_label = Text("Pivot", color="#00FF00", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(pivot_label, 'C4') # Positioned 1 unit away from pivot at C3
        
        # Angle tracking arc
        # Arc is lightweight enough for always_redraw
        angle_arc_dynamic = always_redraw(lambda: Arc(
            radius=0.6,
            start_angle=0,
            angle=angle_tracker.get_value(),
            arc_center=pivot_pos,
            color="#FFFF00"
        ))
        
        self.play(
            Create(pivot_highlight),
            Write(pivot_label),
            FadeIn(angle_arc_dynamic)
        )
        
        # Final rotation to show the full range of states
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(angle_tracker.get_value() + PI), run_time=3)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Pivot Swap", [
            "Watch as the line approaches the next point nearby.",
            "Upon contact, the rotation axis shifts to that point.",
            "The line's direction remains continuous during this transition."
        ])
        
        # === Initialization of Mobjects ===
        
        # Points A and B
        # Point A: Green, Point B: Red
        point_a = Dot(color="#00FF00")
        point_b = Dot(color="#FF0000")
        
        self.place_at_grid(point_a, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(point_b, "D4")
        
        # Labels
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20, color="#00FF00")
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=20, color="#FF0000")
        label_a.next_to(point_a, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_b.next_to(point_b, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # State trackers for rotation and pivot
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(PI/2)  # Starting angle (vertical)
        pivot_mobject = VectorizedPoint(point_a.get_center())
        line_length = 6
        line_color = "#00FFFF"
        
        def get_line_endpoints():
            pivot = pivot_mobject.get_location()
            angle = angle_tracker.get_value()
            direction = np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            start = pivot - (line_length / 2) * direction
            end = pivot + (line_length / 2) * direction
            return [start, end]

        # The rotating line with updater for continuous transformation
        line = Line(*get_line_endpoints(), color=line_color, stroke_width=4)
        line.add_updater(lambda m: m.put_start_and_end_on(*get_line_endpoints()))
        
        # Invisible dots for TracedPath to follow the line tips
        tip1 = Dot(radius=0).add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(get_line_endpoints()[0]))
        tip2 = Dot(radius=0).add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(get_line_endpoints()[1]))
        
        # Sweep trail (faint Yellow)
        trail_color = "#FFFF00"
        trail1 = TracedPath(tip1.get_center, stroke_color=trail_color, stroke_width=2, stroke_opacity=0.3)
        trail2 = TracedPath(tip2.get_center, stroke_color=trail_color, stroke_width=2, stroke_opacity=0.3)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Watch as the line approaches the next point nearby."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(point_a, point_b, label_a, label_b, line, tip1, tip2, trail1, trail2)
        
        # Calculate hitting angle where the line through A meets B
        pos_a = point_a.get_center()
        pos_b = point_b.get_center()
        diff = pos_b - pos_a
        hit_angle = np.arctan2(diff[1], diff[0])
        
        # Rotate clockwise from vertical (PI/2) to the hit_angle
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(hit_angle), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Upon contact, the rotation axis shifts to that point."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # White flash effect at both pivot points
        flash_a = Dot(pos_a, color=WHITE, radius=0.1)
        flash_b = Dot(pos_b, color=WHITE, radius=0.1)
        self.play(
            FadeIn(flash_a), FadeIn(flash_b),
            flash_a.animate.scale(5).set_opacity(0),
            flash_b.animate.scale(5).set_opacity(0),
            run_time=0.6
        )
        self.remove(flash_a, flash_b)
        
        # Shift pivot to point B
        pivot_mobject.move_to(pos_b)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "The line's direction remains continuous during this transition."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Continue clockwise rotation from the same angular direction
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(hit_angle - PI/2), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Reset color of the final lecture line
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with the lecture lines for section 4
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Core Invariant: Counting Sides",
            [
                "Consider the points on each side of the line.",
                "Color points on the left red and right blue.",
                "As the pivot swaps, a point moves through the pivot.",
                "Crucially, the number of points on each side stays constant.",
                "This invariant is the key to solving the problem."
            ]
        )

        # Colors for points, labels, and the rotating line
        COLOR_LEFT_LABEL = "#00FFFF"  # Cyan label for the left side
        COLOR_RIGHT_LABEL = "#FF00FF" # Magenta label for the right side
        COLOR_RED = "#FF0000"        # Left-side points
        COLOR_BLUE = "#0000FF"       # Right-side points
        COLOR_LINE = "#FFFFFF"       # The windmill line

        # Grid positions for points (using a subset of the 6x6 grid)
        # Pivot initially at C3
        pivot_pos = self.grid["C3"]
        # 4 points on the left (x < pivot_x)
        left_pos_keys = ["A2", "B2", "D2", "E2"]
        # 4 points on the right (x > pivot_x)
        right_pos_keys = ["A4", "B4", "D4", "E4"]
        
        # Create point mobjects
        pivot_dot = Dot(pivot_pos, color=WHITE, radius=0.1)
        left_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(self.grid[p], color=WHITE, radius=0.08) for p in left_pos_keys])
        right_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(self.grid[p], color=WHITE, radius=0.08) for p in right_pos_keys])
        
        # Create count labels "4" for each side
        left_label = Text("4", font_size=36, color=COLOR_LEFT_LABEL)
        self.place_at_grid(left_label, "C1")
        right_label = Text("4", font_size=36, color=COLOR_RIGHT_LABEL)
        self.place_at_grid(right_label, "C5")

        # Rotating line setup using ValueTracker for angle and a persistent reference for the pivot
        line_angle = ValueTracker(PI/2) # Start with a vertical orientation
        self.current_pivot_pos = pivot_pos
        
        # Create the line mobject
        rotating_line = Line(ORIGIN, UP, color=COLOR_LINE, stroke_width=2)
        
        # Define a robust updater for the line
        def line_updater(l):
            angle = line_angle.get_value()
            p = self.current_pivot_pos
            direction = np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            # Extend the line symmetrically from the pivot
            l.put_start_and_end_on(p - direction * 3.5, p + direction * 3.5)
            
        rotating_line.add_updater(line_updater)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Consider the points on each side of the line.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(pivot_dot, left_dots, right_dots)
        self.play(Create(rotating_line))
        self.wait(1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Color points on the left red and right blue.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            left_dots.animate.set_color(COLOR_RED),
            right_dots.animate.set_color(COLOR_BLUE),
            Write(left_label),
            Write(right_label)
        )
        self.wait(1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # As the pivot swaps, a point moves through the pivot.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Target point for swap: B4 (at index 1 in right_dots)
        # B4 (3.5, 1.2) from C3 (2.5, 0.2) is at angle PI/4 (45 degrees)
        target_angle_val = PI / 4.0
        
        # Rotate the line clockwise until it hits the target point
        self.play(line_angle.animate.set_value(target_angle_val), run_time=2.0, rate_func=linear)
        
        # Perform the pivot swap:
        # 1. B4 (right side) becomes the new white pivot.
        # 2. C3 (old pivot) moves to the right side and becomes blue.
        # This keeps the total counts (4 Red, 4 Blue) invariant.
        self.play(
            right_dots[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            pivot_dot.animate.set_color(COLOR_BLUE).set_radius(0.08),
            run_time=0.1
        )
        # Update the pivot position used by the line updater
        self.current_pivot_pos = self.grid["B4"]
        
        # Continue the rotation slightly to show the line passing through the new pivot
        self.play(line_angle.animate.set_value(target_angle_val - 0.2), run_time=1.0, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Crucially, the number of points on each side stays constant.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            Flash(left_label, color=COLOR_LEFT_LABEL, flash_radius=0.4),
            Flash(right_label, color=COLOR_RIGHT_LABEL, flash_radius=0.4),
            left_label.animate.scale(1.2),
            right_label.animate.scale(1.2)
        )
        self.play(
            left_label.animate.scale(1.0/1.2),
            right_label.animate.scale(1.0/1.2)
        )
        self.wait(1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This invariant is the key to solving the problem.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Final rotation to emphasize movement
        self.play(line_angle.animate.set_value(target_angle_val - 0.7), run_time=2.0)
        self.wait(2.0)

                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "The 180-Degree Flip"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Now, let the line rotate exactly 180 degrees.",
            "The line returns to its original position in space.",
            "However, its \"left\" and \"right\" sides have now swapped.",
            "Points originally on the left are now on the right.",
            "This requires the sets on both sides to be equal."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        CYAN = "#00FFFF"
        MAGENTA = "#FF00FF"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # Grid-based positions
        pivot_pos = (self.grid["C3"] + self.grid["D4"]) / 2
        
        # Initial Points
        # Side A (initially top, 'left' side) and Side B (initially bottom, 'right' side)
        points_top = VGroup(*[
            Dot(pivot_pos + np.array([x, 0.8, 0]), color=CYAN) for x in [-1.2, 0, 1.2]
        ])
        points_bottom = VGroup(*[
            Dot(pivot_pos + np.array([x, -0.8, 0]), color=MAGENTA) for x in [-1.2, 0, 1.2]
        ])
        
        # Line
        line_length = 4.0
        line = Line(
            pivot_pos + LEFT * (line_length/2),
            pivot_pos + RIGHT * (line_length/2),
            color=CYAN,
            stroke_width=5
        )
        
        # Pivot point dot
        pivot_dot = Dot(pivot_pos, color=WHITE_COLOR, radius=0.08)

        # Angle Tracker
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # Updaters
        def update_line(l):
            angle = angle_tracker.get_value() * DEGREES
            l.set_points_by_ends(
                pivot_pos + rotate_vector(LEFT * (line_length/2), angle),
                pivot_pos + rotate_vector(RIGHT * (line_length/2), angle)
            )
        
        def update_point_color(m, p_pos):
            angle = angle_tracker.get_value() * DEGREES
            # Normal vector to the directed line (rotate_vector(RIGHT, angle))
            # Normal is rotate_vector(UP, angle)
            normal = rotate_vector(UP, angle)
            vec = p_pos - pivot_pos
            # If dot product is positive, it's on the 'left' side of the directed line
            if np.dot(vec, normal) > 0:
                m.set_color(CYAN)
            else:
                m.set_color(MAGENTA)

        line.add_updater(update_line)
        for p in points_top:
            p.add_updater(lambda m, p=p: update_point_color(m, p.get_center()))
        for p in points_bottom:
            p.add_updater(lambda m, p=p: update_point_color(m, p.get_center()))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Now, let the line rotate exactly 180 degrees.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(CYAN)
        self.add(line, pivot_dot, points_top, points_bottom)
        
        initial_label = Text("Initial", font_size=20, color=CYAN)
        self.place_at_grid(initial_label, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(initial_label))
        
        # Continuous rotation through 180 degrees
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(180), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The line returns to its original position in space.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(CYAN)
        
        final_label = Text("Final", font_size=20, color=MAGENTA)
        self.place_at_grid(final_label, "E3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(final_label))
        self.play(Indicate(line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # However, its "left" and "right" sides have now swapped.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(MAGENTA)
        
        # Show swap with visuals
        arrow_top = Arrow(pivot_pos + UP*1.2, pivot_pos + DOWN*1.2, color=WHITE_COLOR, buff=0.1)
        arrow_bottom = Arrow(pivot_pos + DOWN*1.2, pivot_pos + UP*1.2, color=WHITE_COLOR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(line.animate.set_color(MAGENTA))
        self.play(Create(arrow_top), Create(arrow_bottom))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(arrow_top), FadeOut(arrow_bottom))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Points originally on the left are now on the right.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(CYAN)
        
        # Points already have updated colors. Emphasize them.
        self.play(
            *[Flash(p, color=p.get_color(), flash_radius=0.3) for p in points_top],
            *[Flash(p, color=p.get_color(), flash_radius=0.3) for p in points_bottom],
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This requires the sets on both sides to be equal.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Highlight groups to show they are "equal" in concept
        box_top = SurroundingRectangle(points_top, color=MAGENTA, buff=0.2)
        box_bottom = SurroundingRectangle(points_bottom, color=CYAN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(box_top), Create(box_bottom))
        
        # Final pulse effect
        self.play(
            line.animate.scale(1.2).set_stroke(width=8),
            box_top.animate.scale(1.1),
            box_bottom.animate.scale(1.1),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Remove updaters
        line.clear_updaters()
        for p in points_top:
            p.clear_updaters()
        for p in points_bottom:
            p.clear_updaters()
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title = "Conclusion: Infinite Connectivity"
        lines = [
            "- The invariant forces the line to visit every point.",
            "- Each point eventually serves as the windmill's pivot.",
            "- Geometry and combinatorics unite to reveal this elegant pattern."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Define points (fireflies)
        dot_positions = ["C2", "B4", "A5", "D6", "F4", "E2"]
        dots = VGroup()
        for pos in dot_positions:
            dot = Dot(color=BLUE, radius=0.08)
            self.place_at_grid(dot, pos)
            dots.add(dot)
        
        self.add(dots)

        # Windmill line
        self.pivot_idx = 0
        line = Line(LEFT * 3.5, RIGHT * 3.5, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Using a closure-like mechanism with an attribute for the pivot index
        line.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_angle(angle_tracker.get_value()).move_to(dots[self.pivot_idx].get_center()))
        self.add(line)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Speed up rotation through multiple points to show the 'Dance'.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Rotate through dots
        rotation_steps = [
            (1, PI/4), (2, PI/2), (3, 3*PI/4), (4, PI), (5, 5*PI/4), (0, 3*PI/2)
        ]
        
        for idx, angle in rotation_steps:
            self.pivot_idx = idx
            self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(angle), run_time=0.4, rate_func=linear)
        
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Each point eventually serves as the windmill's pivot.
        # Draw the connection path (#FFFF00) formed by the pivots.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Define the connection path
        path_points = [dots[i].get_center() for i in [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0]]
        connection_path = VMobject(color="#FFFF00", stroke_width=4)
        connection_path.set_points_as_corners(path_points)
        
        # Show the connection path being drawn
        self.play(Create(connection_path), run_time=2.5)
        
        # Add glow to all points to show they've been visited
        glow_dots = dots.copy().set_color(YELLOW).set_stroke(width=10, opacity=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(glow_dots))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Geometry and combinatorics unite to reveal this elegant pattern.
        # Fade out all elements except the final connected path.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(dots),
            FadeOut(glow_dots),
            FadeOut(line),
            connection_path.animate.set_stroke(width=6)
        )
        
        # Final emphasis on the path
        self.play(connection_path.animate.scale(1.1), run_time=1)
        self.play(connection_path.animate.scale(0.909), run_time=1)
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Windmill Problem: A Journey through IMO Geometry
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in advanced mathematics and competition logic.

sections.title: Introduction: The Dancing Line
sections.content: Introduce the scenario of a set of finite points in a plane. Define the 'Windmill' process: A line passes through one point (the pivot) and rotates clockwise. When the line hits another point in the set, that new point becomes the pivot, and the rotation continues.
sections.example: Imagine a dark field with several glowing fireflies (points). A single laser beam (the line) starts on one firefly and begins to spin like a clock hand. When it touches another firefly, the laser 'snaps' its center to that new firefly and keeps spinning.

sections.title: Prerequisite: General Position & Rotation
sections.content: Establish the necessary mathematical constraints: No three points are collinear (no 'triple hits') to ensure the pivot swap is unique. Introduce the concept that the line doesn't just rotate—it 'sweeps' the plane, and its orientation is defined by the angle (0 to 180 degrees).
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Forbidden Configuration': Show three points in a straight line and explain why this would cause the 'Windmill' to break (it would hit two points at once). Show a protractor overlaying the pivot to track rotation.

sections.title: Visualizing the Pivot Swap
sections.content: Break down the mechanics of the 'hit and swap.' When the line rotates and hits point 'B' while pivoting on point 'A', the line effectively transitions its rotational axis. Emphasize that the line's direction is continuous even if the pivot changes.
sections.example: Windy the Robot holds a long, straight pole. He stands on point A and spins. As soon as the pole touches point B, Windy teleports to point B and continues spinning the pole from the exact same angle.

sections.title: The Core Invariant: Counting Sides
sections.content: Introduce the 'Aha!' moment—the invariant. If we choose an initial line that divides the remaining points into two sets (S1 on the left, S2 on the right), what happens to the number of points on each side when a pivot swap occurs?
sections.example: Color the points on the left side of the starting line Red and the points on the right side Blue. As the line hits a new point and swaps pivots, show that the number of Red points and Blue points remains constant because the line 'passes through' the point, moving it from one side of the pivot to the other side of the pivot, but keeping it on the same 'half-plane'.

sections.title: The 180-Degree Flip
sections.content: Explain what happens when the line has rotated 180 degrees. The line is the same set of points in space, but its 'direction' is reversed. This means the points that were on the 'left' are now on the 'right.'
sections.example: Use a 'Two-Tone' line (Gold on one side, Silver on the other). After a 180-degree rotation, the Gold side now faces where the Silver side used to face. If there were 'k' points on the left initially, there must be 'k' points on the right now.

sections.title: Conclusion: Infinite Connectivity
sections.content: Conclude that because the number of points on each side stays constant (balanced) relative to the line's orientation, and the line must eventually return to its original position, every point will eventually serve as a pivot.
sections.example: Show a time-lapse of the 'Windmill' completing a full 360-degree cycle. Highlight each firefly as it is touched, showing a 'glow' that stays lit, proving that every single firefly eventually becomes the center of the dance.
